newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher after dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher after dull trade.

text.p: The Stockholm bourse closed firmer on Tuesday but off its day highs with lacklustre trade buoyed in late afternoon by a higher open in New York.
The Stockholm general index edged up 0.43 percent to 2,841.91 in turnover worth 4.05 billion crowns.
"It has been a boring day with low turnover and little buying interest," one broker said.
"Despite that there is a reasonable trend in the market and the U.S. market seems to be going well."
However brokers said Sweden's official decision not to join EMU in 1999 could have a dampening effect on the bourse.
"The effect of the EMU decision is most likely to be seen in the crown that seems to be strengthening and could have a negative impact on exports," a broker said.
The crown firmed to 4.825 to the mark in late trade compared to 4.5120 late Monday.
One of the day's winners was car safety equipment maker Autoliv that closed nine higher at 300.5 crowns after brokerage Alfred Berg issued a buy recommendation on the stock.
Chemicals group Perstorp closed four crowns lower at 121 after posting a 21 percent drop in eight month pre-tax profits and forecasting full year profit down 27 percent.
The drugs sector was one of the top performing sectors rising 1.04 percent, led up by market heavyweight Astra that closed two crowns higher at 130.5 crowns.
Telecoms major Ericsson rose one to 279 crowns.
